title: orjson and msgspec against the repository JSON recipes
question: Do orjson or msgspec write and read the same values as the stdlib identity recipe and the rapidjson exact-decimal recipe?
method: Install orjson 3.13.0, msgspec 0.22.0 and python-rapidjson 1.25 ephemerally and compare encoders over 20,000 generated values per domain, plus fixed encoding and decoding cases.
commands: uv run --no-project --python 3.14.10 --with orjson==3.13.0 --with msgspec==0.22.0 --with python-rapidjson==1.25 --with hypothesis python -I probe.py

results.name: orjson_float_spelling_identical
results.note: Decimal exponents -9 to -5 differ from the stdlib recipe.

results.name: orjson_decodes_integers_beyond_64_bits_exactly
results.note: Returned as float without an error.

results.name: msgspec_number_mismatches_against_rapidjson
results.note: Integers, finite Decimals and text from U+0020.

conclusion: orjson cannot stand behind the identity recipe or serve as a general decoder here: float spelling, refusal behaviour and large-integer decoding differ. msgspec reproduces the exact-decimal recipe on finite values apart from control-character escapes. Which values production code hashes is outside this probe.
consumed_by: orjson-json-codec review opportunities O01, O08 and O09
